feature: Captions and Transitions where a video editor expects them
summary: On a video the panel now shows Captions only with nothing or the captions picked, and the Transitions tiles only with a cut picked. A picked clip, title, sound or graphic shows its own sections and nothing else. A new video's Library folds back once something is on the timeline, so the first thing you draw gets the room.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The laptop window is 1200 by 720 (the walks use it).

try.do: Open a recording and click empty canvas so nothing is picked. The panel shows Time, then Captions, then the Library folded. There is no Transitions section.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the clip on the timeline. Its Properties, Time, Appearance, Effects and Audio sections show, then the Library. No Captions, no Transitions.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press B, cut the clip, then click the cut. The cut's Properties show with the Transitions tiles under them, open.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Escape. The Transitions section goes with the cut. To drag a transition with no cut picked, open the Library, pick Catalog, then Transitions.
Add a piece of music and click it. Channel and Fades are on screen without scrolling, with no Captions under them.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: File > New Video. The Library is open on Media. Draw a line with the Line tool: the Library folds to its header and the line's Appearance, Width included, is on screen.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the Captions row on the timeline of a captioned recording. The Captions section (style, cue, timing) shows as the captions' own.

evaluate: With a clip picked, do you miss Captions under it, or is the menu bar and the clip's right click (Add Captions) enough?
With nothing picked, is the Library's Transitions kind an obvious enough place to find a transition to drag?
With a cut picked, do the Transitions tiles under the cut's Properties read as the place to pick one, the way Premiere's Effects panel does?
After a new video, does the Library folding back when the first thing lands feel right, or should it stay open?
rough: Before: Captions (its whole style form once captions exist) and a folded Transitions header sat under every pick, so a picked arrow or line carried the document's captions under its own rows; a sound's Fades and a line's Appearance fell under the fold on smaller windows.

Matches both mocks: the Transitions tiles sit under a picked cut as video-transitions.html draws them, and in the Library's Transitions kind as video-library.html draws it. They show twice only while a cut is picked AND the Library is opened on Catalog > Transitions; otherwise in one place at a time.

The tiles section is headed Transitions where video-transitions.html heads its group Effects with Transitions as its count; settled by the-panel-has-a-transitions-group-of-tiles-as-th, which named it.
A Library opened by hand on a video still takes about 40 to 50 per cent of the panel where video.html caps its body at 118px; filed as a-video-s-library-opened-by-hand-stays-a-short-s.
With a cut picked on the laptop window, the cut's Properties take about half the panel and the Transitions tiles show one row before scrolling; same follow-up does not cover it, left in the task log.
